newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Red Cross calls for end to air raids on Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross calls for end to air raids on Kabul.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross called on Thursday on the warring parties in Afghanistan to stop air raids and shelling on civilian areas.

"The International Committee of the Red Cross calls on all the warring parties to respect and to refrain from inflicting pain on the civilian population of Kabul through indescriminate air attacks and shelling." said Thomas Gurtner, deputy head of the Red Cross delegation in Kabul.
A plane of the anti-Taleban alliance dropped a bomb on a building in central Kabul on Thursday, killing three people and wounding three others.
The bomb hit a building close to the presidential palace that the Taleban were using as a guest house. Witnesses said that at least one of the dead was a passer-by.
Gurtner also referred to recent air raids which hit civilian areas in the north of Kabul.

"In Khair Khana, a northern suburb of Kabul city, on Sunday 20th and Wednesday 23rd...cluster bombs were dropped into areas causing the deaths of six civilians while 25 others had to be treated in hospitals monitored by the International Committee of the Red Cross." he said.

"The International Committee of the Red Cross solemnly appeals to all parties to use their utmost restraint and to make sure that civilian lives be spared during this period of heightened tension and conflict."
Opposition forces have been increasing pressure on the Taleban, who hold Kabul. On Thursday, the opposition moved within 12 miles (20 km) of the Afghan capital.
The opposition gains put them within rocketing range of the city for the first time in nine months.
At least six rockets hit an area of open ground close to the airport in northeastern Kabul on Thursday.

Opposition forces have been moving steadily closer to Kabul for the last five days since they erupted from bases at the north end of the valley that runs from the city to the foothills of the Hindu Kush mountains.
